claim: Venezuela TPS EADs, I-797 notices and I-94s issued on or before Feb 5, 2025 with an Oct 2, 2026 expiration remain valid until Oct 2, 2026.

plan_value: Docs issued on or before 2/5/2025 showing Oct 2, 2026 expiration valid only until Oct 2, 2026
correction_note: Confirmed; wording tightened: the rule covers EADs, Forms I-797 and Forms I-94 that were issued on or before Feb 5, 2025 with an Oct 2, 2026 expiration. USCIS says "until October 2, 2026" (its filing table says "through Oct. 2, 2026"). Cal. 3:25-cv-01766) is still being litigated; no primary source found extending past Oct 2, 2026. Deadline is 7 days away.

claim: Starting Oct 1, 2026, H.R.1 (P.L. 119-21) §71109 ends federal Medicaid/CHIP matching for full coverage for noncitizens other than LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants (citizens and nationals are unaffected), with exceptions for emergency Medicaid and the CHIPRA 214 lawfully-residing children/pregnant women option.
quote: beginning on October 1, 2026, except as provided in paragraphs (2) and (4), in no event shall payment be made to a State under this section for medical assistance furnished to an individual unless such individual is—
plan_value: Medicaid/CHIP noncitizen eligibility change starts Oct 1, 2026
correction_note: Date confirmed from the statute. Precision fix: §71109 limits FEDERAL PAYMENT (FFP) to states rather than directly rewriting eligibility. Groups that remain: citizens and nationals, LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants, COFA migrants. Everyone else (e.g., refugees, asylees, parolees, trafficking victims unless they hold one of those statuses) loses federally matched full-scope Medicaid/CHIP. Exceptions: 1903(v)(2) emergency Medicaid and 1903(v)(4) CHIPRA 214 lawfully residing children/pregnant women option. States may still pay with state-only funds. CMS SHO #26-001 (Apr 8, 2026) names "asylees, refugees, parolees, or victims of trafficking", but that was seen in search results only: medicaid.gov returned 403 to the box and WebFetch timed out, so there is no CMS quote in the ledger. Florida's CHIPRA 214 election and AHCA plans are unsourced.

claim: Florida counties (125.0156) and municipalities (166.246) may not fund ID cards for people without proof of lawful presence, and may not accept IDs from issuers that knowingly issue to people not lawfully present; federal documents are exempt.
quote: A municipality may not: (1) Provide funds to any person, entity, or organization for the purpose of issuing an identification card or document to an individual who does not provide proof of lawful presence in the United States. (2) Accept as identification any identification card or document issued by any person, entity, or organization that knowingly issues such identification cards or documents to individuals who are not lawfully present in the United States. This prohibition does not apply to any documentation issued by, or on behalf of, the Federal Government.
correction_note: Discovery said the statutes 'limit which IDs local governments can accept'. Precisely: counties and cities may not accept an ID from an issuer that knowingly issues IDs to people not lawfully present, and may not fund such IDs. Documents issued by or for the Federal Government are exempt. Identical text in 125.0156 for counties (https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2026/125.0156). History: ch. 2023-40, ch. 2024-9.
